newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Jakarta share prices ended lower on Thursday following falls in market heavyweight Telkom despite selective foreign buying of some blue-chips, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index fell 3.77 points, or 0.62 percent, to close at 602.99 points, off an intra-day low of 601.70 points. Losers led gainers by 61 to 46, with 61 counters unchanged.
Analyts said some blue-chips and small-sized counters can make further gains in coming days and it could help the index consolidate above the 600-point resistance level.
"Some unsucsesful bidders for Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) stock who received refunds today could be moving it into other stock tomorrow," a foreign analyst said.

But, she added, the amount will be limited because investors may await BNI's listing on Monday following its hugely successful float earlier this month. The listing is widely expected to provide a boost to the market.

Brokers said they expect Telkom's price in New York to rebound tonight, which could help sentiment in Jakarta on Friday. "Technically at this level, some bargain hunters will eat the stock up," a foreign broker said.
Telkom fell 50 rupiah to 3,800, off a low of 3,750 rupiah on a volume of 4.6 million shares.
Telecommunications cable maker Voksel Electic topped the active list with 9.4 million shares traded, rising 25 rupiah to 1,050 rupiah after hitting a high of 1,200 rupiah by midday.
Brokers said the active buying was due to talk of a possible merger which was later confirmed by a company official.

A company official told Reuters that negotiations on extending Voksel's activities to related businesses were on, but no decision had yet been arrived at. He said Voksel is considering a merger with another firm as part of the plans.
Chemical firm Aneka Kimia was also actively traded on reports that it would set up joint ventures with foreign partners.
Aneka financial director Sutirta Budiman told Reuters that the firm is negotiating with several foreign companies to set up joint ventures to manufacture chemical products.
"We are holding serious negotiations. We expect to finalise one deal by the end of 1996. We expect to disclose (announce) another two or three joint ventures next year," he said.
Aneka Kimia rose 325 rupiah, or 28.89 percent, to 1,450 on a volume of 3.7 million shares.
Blue-chips including vehicle maker Astra International, toll operator Citra Marga and conglomerate Bimantara were among the targets of foreign buyers, brokers said.
Astra International rose 125 rupiah to 4,550 on a volume of 1.3 million shares while Citra Marga rose 100 rupiah to 2,125 on 2.4 million shares.
Brokers said sentiment on Citra Marga improved partly due to a report that one of its shareholders had won a contract to build a toll road in Central Java.
